name: go-diskfs-portable-filesystem-space-accounting
instr:
go-diskfs lacks a portable, byte-based view of filesystem usage. Add capacity, physical allocation, logical content, file counts, inode availability, and accounting certainty for partition queries, copy planning, and reconciliation, without changing existing contents, mutations, serialization, reads, writes, or copy errors.

Every ext4, fat12, fat16, fat32, iso9660, and squashfs `FileSystem` must expose deterministic `Usage` from native metadata, or return an error without a plausible partial report or concrete-type assertion. Exact reports use overflow-safe unsigned arithmetic and balance allocated and available bytes against bounded capacity. Estimates never exceed that capacity.

FAT accounting follows clusters, including reserved entries, duplicated tables, fixed-root storage, rounding, and released chains. ext4 reconciles block-group counters, reserved blocks, inodes, sparse files, and directory growth. Mutable ISO9660 and SquashFS workspaces are estimated. Reopened serialized images use exact native allocation, including ISO extents and overhead or SquashFS compressed storage, independently of logical bytes.

`Disk.FilesystemUsage` preserves whole-disk results, bounds partition and `backend.SubStorage` results to the selected range, and rejects missing partitions or inconsistent geometry. Different partition offsets must produce equivalent range-bounded reports without changing byte translation.
